feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: What Democrats plan to prioritize if they retake the House
entry.summary: This election will determine control of Congress. Rep. Pete Aguilar, who represents California's 33rd Congressional District, shares how Democratic Party leaders are feeling as results come in.

entry.title: Legendary photographer on getting that perfect election night picture
entry.summary: On election night, photographers will be in position, ready to snap history-making moments. It's something Pulitzer-prize-winner photographer David Hume Kennerly, has done for decades.

entry.title: Japan faces diplomatic dilemma amid joint pressure from nuclear neighbors
entry.summary: As the Ukraine war grinds on, ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo wants more support from Washington, but some Japanese are concerned they may not get it.

entry.title: Election Day 2026: The view from Iowa
entry.summary: Iowa has become an unexpected state to watch this midterm election.

entry.title: Voters explain how they feel about the economy as midterms draw to a close
entry.summary: The cost of living was a major issue for voters this year. NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with three people about how they're feeling the effects of inflation as the midterms come to an end.

entry.title: It's been the most expensive election yet, though political ads aren't that effective
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with political scientist John Sides of Vanderbilt University about the record political ad spending this election, despite the limited effectiveness of political ads.

entry.title: While votes are counted, NPR's film critic thinks about counting in movies
entry.summary: Stressed by waiting for election results? Hollywood offers dozens of less nerve-wracking ways to count.

entry.title: Supreme Court leans toward LGBTQ exclusion for publicly funded Catholic preschools
entry.summary: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday about Colorado's universal pre-K program and whether religious schools can bar certain families despite the state's anti-discrimination law.

entry.title: Western Kentucky welcomes data centers in hopes they make up for coal losses
entry.summary: In Kentucky's former coal country, data centers are a welcome sight as people hope they will bring in money.

entry.title: Election Day 2026: The view from Texas
entry.summary: We're hearing from NPR reporters around the country on Election Day, including in Texas, which has had a tough Senate race.
